conviction_note: Today is day two of the sell-off after CervoMed's 2026-10-12 open-label nfvPPA biomarker release (-22.05% on 10-12, -11.1% at the screen on 2.25x volume). I found nothing dated in the window and no mechanism that would close an overshoot. Two supply facts roughly offset each other: the baby-shelf cap is nearly used up, so a new primary offering is unlikely, but PIPE shares bought at $3.14 are resale-registered and underwater. The scaled number therefore stays near zero with a slight lean to the name's own history (39.5% up, median -1.99%) and its high ATR. impact_sum (-0.2) and impact_scaled (-0.48) agree in sign and are similar in size.

cause.label: clinical_or_binary_readout
cause.what_happened: On 2026-10-12 CervoMed released initial 12-week open-label plasma biomarker data from its 25-patient Phase 2a nfvPPA trial (a late-breaking oral at ISFTD). Mean NfL fell about 3.1 pg/mL from a 45.7 pg/mL baseline, GFAP was stable, there was no control arm and no clinical endpoint, and one patient discontinued for elevated liver enzymes. The stock fell 22% that day. It is down another ~11% today, almost all intraday and with no new company filing beyond the Item 7.01/8.01 8-K furnishing that release on 10-13.

The ISFTD late-breaker was pre-announced on 2026-09-10, so the event date was known in advance

findings.finding: The company has used almost all of its baby-shelf (S-3 I.B.6) capacity: the June 2026 424B5 put public float at $32.1m (cap about $10.7m per 12 months), and the $10.0m registered direct closed 2026-06-22. A meaningful ATM draw or shelf takedown into the window is therefore close to impossible, which removes the most common second shoe for a small-cap biotech after weak data.
findings.mechanism_in_window: This is a standing constraint over the whole window (the 12-month I.B.6 lookback runs to June 2027). It is what does NOT land tonight: no 424B5 ATM or shelf takedown of size can price before the 10-14 close. Cash of $24.9m with runway to Q3 2027 (10-Q) also means there is no forced raise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The June 2026 financings (PIPE on 06-10, RD on 06-18/22) came during the 06-10 (-22.15%) and 06-17 (-15.71%) falls, which were followed by +8.44% and +11.29% next closes in the baseline history.
findings.why_not_priced: The base rate's negative drift is mostly second-shoe dilution. If the tape were pricing an imminent raise, the 22% and 11% falls would sit beside a fresh 424B5 or an 8-K. The shelf arithmetic rules out a material one, but a reader of the tape does not see that arithmetic.
findings.independence: The 10-Q states no ATM activity in 2026 under the Leerink sales agreement, and cash of $24.9m with runway through Q3 2027: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1053691/000143774926026592/crvo20260630_10q.htm

findings.finding: 3,360,377 PIPE units bought at $3.14 on 2026-06-11 are resale-registered (S-3 effective 2026-07-10, 424B3) and now sit about 29% underwater at $2.23. After a disappointing readout, those holders are a seller who can keep selling into the next session.
findings.mechanism_in_window: The resale registration is effective, so these shares can be sold on any session, including 10-14. That kind of exit is a known continuation channel on a second day of post-data selling.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On two-day sequences in the baseline, 06-23 (-9.93%) was followed by -12.37% and then +2.76%, and 05-15 by -11.63% and then -4.93%. The history is mixed, with continuation slightly more common.
findings.why_not_priced: Today's 2.25x volume, on a day with no new company news, looks like holders still exiting. Nothing says that seller is done. If the supply were exhausted, the second day would have been flat on low volume rather than -11% intraday.
findings.independence: The 10-Q gives the PIPE terms ($3.14 units with Series B warrants at $3.32 and Series C at $3.14, both out of the money now): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1053691/000143774926026592/crvo20260630_10q.htm.
